read_scope.notes: Read the entire 22-page PDF, including references and Appendices A–G, using page-separated text extraction and visual inspection of every page. Inspected Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–10; enlarged page 17 to resolve an apparent low-resolution spacing artifact. Read the frozen paper.tex and consulted frozen included TeX for results and table notation. Technical appendices were treated as optional depth when assessing the main narrative. Independently verified the PDF SHA256 before and after reading. Confirmed 22 PDF pages and a 155-word abstract by whitespace count of the TeX abstract after accent/percent normalization. No other reviews, earlier versions, progress records, goals, repository evidence, or non-snapshot manuscript were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with clear local definitions and unusually effective transitions from intuition to notation. Section 4.1 explains contrasts through the Monet–Sisley lightness gap and distinguishes aligned response from total error before presenting equations. Section 5 consistently names the statistic, direction, reference target and qualification needed to interpret each result. The abstract could name total contrast error more explicitly, and the discussion could replace one abstract reporting recommendation with a concrete synthesis; these are localized refinements rather than recurrent comprehension obstacles.
score_reasons.structure: The question, reference panel, six prompt conditions, feature representation, two primary scores and inferential family form a coherent progression. Results have informative, finding-led headings and clearly separate the declared comparisons from retrospective pair, calibration and source diagnostics. Detailed derivations, controls and older interventions are appropriately confined to appendices, so the main account stands alone. The brief discussion is coherent but could use its existing space to synthesize the model tradeoff more concretely before the limitations.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The intended reader can recover the experiment and its bounded target without repository consultation: 649 digital reproductions, four equally weighted painter means, a separate scaling panel, 14 identical scene briefs and six clauses with two repeats are explicit. Table 1 provides intuitive feature interpretations; Section 4 gives a real lightness example and the 1/0/1 error examples; captions identify benchmarks, signs, projections and descriptive status. Calibration is explained as one scalar fitted on other scenes without image alteration. The main remaining refinement is that the standalone abstract uses generic outperform/error wording where total contrast error would make the positive-alignment versus no-distinction comparison more immediately intelligible.
score_reasons.engagement: The opening Monet-versus-Sisley example makes the question consequential, Figure 1 supplies an inspectable visual intervention, and Figures 2–3 reveal which painter distinctions drive the aggregate scores. The GPT Image 2 alignment/error contrast and the two ordering changes in Section 5.4 supply a clear narrative without hype. Main figures are legible at adequate rendering resolution and their captions reward inspection. The discussion currently ends the interpretive development quickly and moves into limitations; a concrete synthesis using the already reported FLUX/GPT Image 2 contrast would give the ending greater force without adding length.

strengths: The abstract is standalone, exactly 155 words by the stated count, and includes the design, reference target, dominant shared change, unresolved benchmark comparison, retrospective pair result, calibration change and perceptual limit.

Section 4.1 makes the central method accessible through an actual median-lightness comparison and idealized generators with expected errors 1, 0 and 1; the ensuing equations therefore formalize an already understandable distinction.

Figure 1 shows all six conditions for all six generators with an explicit reading order and honest historical-reference provenance; Figure 2 uses consistent axes and magnified M/S/P detail; Figure 3 gives values and benchmark markers rather than relying on color alone.

Tables 2–4 and their surrounding prose distinguish point-estimate ordering, simultaneous intervals, the theoretical no-distinction predictor and retrospective calibration/source sensitivity. The changed Sunburst comparison is visible rather than buried.

The main text explains why scene-dependent painter differences can raise error against a pooled historical target without calling that variation an artistic failure, and keeps optional estimator and historical-cohort detail outside the main narrative.

findings.location: Abstract, page 1, sentences beginning “All models show positive alignment” and “We uniformly rescale”
findings.issue: The abstract names alignment but describes the competing criterion only as outperforming a predictor and later as error. The main text explains that this is total disagreement of measured painter contrasts, including additional directions, but the standalone abstract leaves that distinction implicit.
findings.reader_effect: A new reader may briefly read positive alignment as successful recovery and find the failure to outperform a no-distinction predictor paradoxical, or interpret the later error ordering as a broader quality ranking.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the alignment sentence with a version that names the criterion, for example: “All models align positively with reference differences, yet none demonstrably lowers total contrast error below a predictor ignoring painter distinctions.” This replaces the original sentence without increasing its whitespace word count, preserving the 155-word abstract ceiling; the main-text explanation can remain as written.

findings.issue: The discussion gives sound reporting recommendations but stops short of restating the concrete tradeoff that made those recommendations necessary. Its sentence about whether a comparison permits a strength adjustment largely repeats what Section 5.4 and Table 3 have already explained procedurally.
findings.reader_effect: The closing interpretation is more abstract than the engaging results: readers must themselves reconnect FLUX’s lower original error, its Cézanne-dependent alignment and GPT Image 2’s stronger but oversized contrasts to the proposed reporting practice.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the final procedural sentence of the paragraph, or compress the paragraph, with one concrete synthesis of those already reported findings: FLUX’s restrained contrasts have lower original error, whereas GPT Image 2 becomes lowest after strength calibration. Keep the descriptive status and fixed feature/reference scope, and use replacement text rather than adding a paragraph so the manuscript stays within 22 pages.

summary: An excellent and self-contained editorial presentation of a bounded digital-reference comparison. The main narrative explains the measurements, benchmarks, uncertainty and retrospective diagnostics clearly, and the figures make the distinctions inspectable. No consequential overstatement or missing main-text explanation was identified. Remaining changes are localized wording and closing-synthesis refinements, not a need for new experiments or a broader claim.
